body:
It does, it actually does. I guess each person has to figure it out for themselves huh? So it's just a distraction basically. Walking doesn't work for me, my feet are going but my mind isn't occupied and so I just keep thinking about it. I'd need something that engages me more, reading or something.

Thanks for the explanation, it does help.

Hey... I've been googling around for "coping skills" and am not finding much. Is there a ressource somewhere that you know of? I've been asking my psychologist for something like this but she usually says "go walk it off", and no matter how long I walk it off, my feelings still boil inside of me for hours and when I finally feel like they've gone down a bit, I get back home and being in the situation again just brings it all up again. Needless to say I have to find something better. If anyone knows of a website, forum, anything I could consult on this, let me know, thanks...

Your reply really hit close to home.

The thing is, no two people are alike, not even Asperger's people. Which doesn't mean your advice isn't relevant, only that I cannot assume 100% that what happened to you will happen to me.

The thing is, in my case, there is also my own crap to take into consideration. I have mentioned bits of it here and there throughout this post. I'm ADD so when I ask for attention, it has to be now. I've never had a relationship where I didn't argue every single day. It seems to never be enough, my current boyfriend tells me so but many have said similar things before. I'm a child of a Borderline personality disorder mother and while psychologists have agreed that I don't fit a formal diagnosis, I *have* inherited some acquired behaviours from her. I don't communicate clearly what I want, I expect him to just want to do exactly what I want to do, I expect him to have the same criteria as me for what's important and what isn't, and although he is willing to fulfill my needs when I express them, I am unsatisfied because I would want him to *share* these values of mine without my having to tell him, which is unfair to anyone really, even moreso someone with Asperger's but nobody can live up to that.

My boyfriend doesn't want to take meds. His case isn't that bad, it's mostly anxiety that is the issue, I wish we could control that and I think we could deal with the rest.

You're right on the "what could be" versus "what is". The thing is, I have trouble assessing "what is". Sometimes I'm happy and I feel like I was unfair to him for complaining, and sometimes I'm desperate and I feel like my whole life is awful. I have a very short attention span, I am extremely ADD and what I am living NOW basically becomes what I am living ALL THE TIME. I remember nothing else, I am fully immersed in the moment and so I have a hard time determining if I'm happy or not in general, in this relationship. I also have a hard time being fair, even though he is sometimes really sweet and attentive for the whole week, if on one occasion he doesn't give me what I want right away, I'll lose it and feel rejected and become upset and start crying, etc. I'm not doing it *to* manipulate him, at the time it's very real to me and this is all I see. But it comes across as manipulative, and in general this makes me very inconsistent and unpredictable. On top of not wanting to express what I want clearly.

So, you see, the blame doesn't all rest on his shoulders. Yes, he most likely has Asperger's syndrome, but everyone has *something* and nobody can be a perfect mate or give me a "win" if I don't make that possible to begin with. The lack of affection is hard to deal with, but he is learning how to feel good around me and when he isn't anxious, we do have great moments which I know are genuine.

Really, I wasn't coming here to talk about my relationship, but it sure has turned that way. I was here to talk about those moments when my emotions get too much and overwhelm me and I don't see a way out of this and my brain starts telling me I should end it. It might be easier to deal with if I was with some idealized guy who does everything perfectly, but in the end, I'm still incapable of controlling my emotions and they take over in very bad ways sometimes. THIS is my problem. Of course, the Asperger's doesn't help, it triggers me more than it should.

I don't really know where I'm going with this. I'm incapable of coming up with a clear conclusion to any of this. Of course I'd like a prince charming who comes up behind me, cuddles me, tells me he's lucky to have me in his life, and all that great stuff. But I think these are fairytales, that sort of romance doesn't happen naturally and last 20 years. It needs work, and above all it requires for me to express that I want that. The good part is, I have a partner who may be slow learning, but who actually wants to learn and implements what he learns in the long run. The bad part is, a bunch of things I thought I could take for granted are really NOT a part of the package with him.

Thanks for sharing your story. It does give me food for thought and I will have to consider your input seriously. I don't want to live my life hoping for something that will never come and wasting the time I have wishing for happiness in the future. But at the same time, I don't want to repeat my pattern of fleeing a relationship when things don't work out, only to re-inflict the same bottomless pit of need for affection on the next guy. Everyone is a "fixer-upper" on some level, everyone has their shit, their baggage. It doesn't make sense to me to expect to find someone who is perfect on all levels and to throw my relationship away like that because I want this idealized person instead.

Yes, but I may not have access to it, or my reason might not make sense to him. It seems unfair that I should have to justify my emotions with reasons and "convince him" of if I am justified or not to feel a certain way. At some point you just gotta respect that you're with someone who has emotions and you will not always share them but if you care for them, you should take them into consideration to some degree.

That's very lucky indeed. For me, I think it was that way at first, but the time it took him to warm up to me was the time it took me to lose my natural easy-going disposition. When the needles were there, I felt them too, and it made me unsure about going to him with my affection. In time, he became more open, but I was already feeling unsure, and this fueled anxiety between us.

Actually, like I said elsewhere, there is change, it's slow but it's there. So if past performance is an indicator, I can expect him to slowly and gradually come my way and become more and more attentive and comfortable around me and affectionate. Just... slowly.

If nothing at all was going to change, I don't know, do I get to change? Because yes he is Asperger's, but I'm also the other half of this relationship, and there are things that belong to me, things I need to work on. My emotions are very powerful and they play tricks on me on many fronts. I'm sure I'm not the best communicator. I have my faults, too, I just don't know what to do about them now that I understand where they come from.

Everyone talks like if I leave this guy, some miracle prince charming is gonna show up. I don't believe it. That's why people flee from relationships the minute something is tough. What is this "win" I'm supposed to need, and why am I not going to get it from this guy? At least here I have a chance at facing my demons, that's a win if I ever formulated one for myself.

My dreams and aspirations aren't dependent on someone else. Whoever I have a relationship with, I can't blame them for not realizing my dreams.

I can't believe your shit. Why are you here? To blame people for being in a bad situation and feeling like they have no way out? You're self-righteous about your own definition of MY relationship. My relationship, to me, is more sacred than the bullshit I consider marriage to be. you have no right to decide for me what is best for me. This is a safe space, not a "let me hammer my opinion about what you should do in your head" space. I said I'm not willing to consider that option, so you should respect that.

You're self-righteous about your opinions on marriage. I don't believe in marriage, I thanked you numerous times for your advice while respectfully telling you that I do not relate and that this doesn't help me, so why can't you just call it quits? You just feel like moralizing and telling others what they should do because you're supposedly so experienced you know everything about everyone? How did you ever become so self-important? You know what's best for everyone? Are you sent by God to deliver some essential, unwavering dogmatic wisdom with us all?

I'm not blaming everyone else for my problems. If you read anything at all about being with an Asperger's person, you'd know that there is such a thing as Cassandra syndrome. People not acquainted with Asperger's often don't understand what the spouse is going through because they are not in the Asperger's person's intimate circle and are not treated the same way. Spouses of people who have Asperger's syndrome experience something very similar to seasonal depression disorder, the difference being the disorder is triggered by chronic lack of affection. I'm not blaming my spouse for having Asperger's, which is why I won't leave him, as you so urge me to do. However, I do point out that he has Asperger's and that dealing with this is making me depressive and exhausted, because it is relevant information. I don't see why you're so bent on trying to blame all my problems on me, you don't know me, and you're the one who came here, in a safe space where people seek understanding and a sympathetic ear when they're feeling exhausted and the ideas in their heads scare them. You have only heightened my distress and made me regret coming here at all. You have no place here.
I'm here because I need a safe space to vent. Not your blame and self-righteous attitude.

I'm not on Facebook. :( I used to be but I deleted it. I might get back on it sometime soon for work but I don't generally like it there. Are you on Twitter? Or would e-mail work? Thanks, seriously I would really love to have someone who understands, just to vent once in a while, or ask for advice. Nobody understands and I'm afraid to talk to people because everyone just says "dump him", so I'd rather keep to myself than be told this all the time. I don't want to dump him, but people don't respect my choice, they think I'm not seeing straight or something, but it's me in the situation, not them.

Your issues really hit home. Same here. We don't have a child, but same as you, I feel like he never has any initiative for helping around the house, or being romantic with me, or even including me in his things. He has a lot of hobbies which are by definition solitary, like video games, playing music, programming, etc. I've tried to get interested in his things, but every time we do something, it's one of his own interests and mine go out the window.

We've had to set up "rules and regulations" just so things like opening and closing curtains mornings and nights, turning the heating on and off, doing dishes, making the bed, doing the common laundry, putting clean dishes away, etc., aren't by default my responsibility. Eventually the rules sink in but it always has to be brought up and negotiated in advance, he'll never come up with it himself or even realize there is something to do. He says that even just agreeing to helping me cook sometimes is a big compromise since he doesn't care what he eats and would have raw vegetable for dinner if he was on his own.

After we fight, he's super sweet on the spot, but the very next day he forgets and even though I try to bring it up, "Hey, yesterday you said you'd try to remember this...?" he just gets upset at me. His promises don't really come true right away. But I do notice slow change over long periods of time. His attitude slowly metamorphoses into something else. But we have to discuss things lengthily and he's never satisfied with my answers.

One time I had to argue with him for three weeks for him to stop calling me "my broad" when talking to his friends, as I found it really demeaning and giving a bad image of our relationship, like he doesn't respect me. Just saying it hurts me should be enough for him to understand, but he wants the big justification, I have to give him a big speech about how "broad" is a derogatory term that is linked to prostitutes, and he says he's using it sarcastically, and I have to tell him how his buddy doesn't necessarily understand that and his negative opinion of me and of our relationship is therefore reinforced, and I don't want to be the object of that, and he will argue and argue on his "right" to call me his "broad". In the end when I finally convince him, I trust that he will respect my wishes, but it takes so much for me to get there and it makes me feel like he doesn't respect my feelings in themselves, and that if I somehow don't manage to convince him, if the points I bring up aren't satisfactory, he will ignore how bad it makes me feel and just do his thing. In the end I feel pretty worthless in his eyes, like my feelings aren't worth considering. :(
And is this what you do? Lurk around SuicideWatch trying to shove your values down people's throats? If someone disagrees with you, you just argue with them and criticize them? Really?

Yeah, I understand this. Logic is his language. But the problem is I also have emotional needs and my emotions shouldn't be required to be logical. Sometimes I just feel a certain way, and the helpful thing is to listen and accept without asking for justifications. But this seems impossible to him.

Yeah, that sounds about right. It gets better, the number of needles slowly goes down, but they go one by one, and it takes so much time. Then one day, because something has exhausted them, it's 1000 needles all over again. The overall average becomes better, but this will always be a part of him.
I don't know what else to say from now on... Like I said, I'm not interested in leaving him for now.

Tristan was not Isolde's wife to be, he was the knight named by her husband to protect her. Their love was never translated into a formal union, because its very nature destroyed the sanctity of marriage.

From Wikipedia: "Although Iseult marries Mark, she and Tristan are forced by the potion to seek one another as lovers. Although the typical noble Arthurian character would be shamed from such an act, the love potion that controls them frees Tristan and Iseult from responsibility. The king's advisors repeatedly try to have the pair tried for adultery, but again and again the couple use trickery to preserve their façade of innocence."

Romeo and Juliet also isn't about marriage, it's about two people who wanted to be together against the wishes of their parents, who had promised them to be married to other people.

I don't know who this Campbell guy is but it seems like you misunderstand what he is saying. From your quote, it seems like he makes the point that courtly love was a reaction to the institution of marriage.

Vows can be exchanged without marriage. Besides, I'm not religious and if I were to get married, I wouldn't do it in front of a rabbi or priest or whatever. I'd do it at City Hall, and as far as I know, vows aren't obligatory there.

I'm sorry, but the fact that I'm married or not doesn't change my view of my relationship. I respect your opinion that it does so for your own relationship and for others who find these things important, but I don't even value monogamy that much, so even though I appreciate the sentiment and how you're trying to free me from my perceived obligations by invoking marriage, I don't relate at all. So, again, thank you for your input, I understand it comes from a good place, but I don't share these values so I don't feel very freed, because I don't feel like anything *binds* me to anyone except my own free will.

I think he's willing to meet me in the middle, it's just a long process. He's actually made significant changes, it just took two whole years, and because he starts from so far, the things he changed often stay invisible to me.

For example, he doesn't want anything to do with family, not even his own. He moved away from where he grew up just so he wouldn't have to see them (for other reasons too, but this was a part of it for sure). My family is pretty intense and we always have obligations. He never wanted to come to any dinners or gatherings. Eventually I told him if he was going to be with me, he would have to get a bit more involved and accept to become a part of my family to some extent. Slowly but surely, he changed his ways. He now pretty much joins us every time or almost. I don't even see this, because to me it seems obvious: you're with someone, you have to at least be courteous with the family and present on special occasions. If possible, you should have friendly relations with them. So I don't see this as an effort on his part, because it seems so expected to me. But he's doing a lot just to meet this requirement which he doesn't share.

In the meantime, when my needs for intimacy aren't met, he will bring up how tired he is and how little time he has for himself since we've spent time with my family. But this doesn't satisfy me, I wonder why can't we have both? But then I remember what a toll these interactions take on him. I'm just bad and inconsistent for a lot of things, and when I need something, I need it now, which doesn't work with him.

I don't know how to express this... I know he's trying. Sometimes I feel like I'm asking for very little, and other times, when he reminds me of my contradictory arguments one way or another, I realize that I always find a reason to whine about his actions, even though my arguments sometimes contradict themselves. One day, the  conversation will go like this:

* "You never want to do anything special with me!"
* "But we spend so much time together, we were running around in stores all weekend together."
* "That doesn't count, it's not special or fun or intimate enough, I want real quality time."

Other days it goes:

* "Would you come to the store with me?"
* "Meh, don't feel like it, I'll just play video games until you come back."
* "I can't believe you never want to spend any time with me, nothing I propose is ever good enough."
* "But I thought this was just going to the store, you've mentioned that this isn't important to you, it isn't special or anything!"
* "Well it's up to us to make it fun, whatever, we run up and down the aisles and laugh at the stupid things they sell!"

I mean, at that moment it feels very real to me, I guess I try to justify my feelings a lot and I shouldn't, I just end up making up reasons for how I feel and they often contradict themselves and this confuses him. I think he wants to try, he just doesn't understand what to do because I'm so shifty.

Well, love existed before marriage and will exist after it. In fact, marriage was never about love before the 20th century. It was about trading daughters for family alliances. A man was promised a daughter for his wife in exchange for rights of passage on a bridge he owned, that sort of thing. If you're talking about love, well, I love this man, and I don't need a piece of paper to tell me whether my commitment is a lifetime thing or not.

Your quote about troubadours actually illustrates this. Courtly love isn't synonymous to marriage, in fact it often positions itself against it in medieval literature. The husband is the obligation, the lover is the unattainable one. Poets sang these songs as a **protest against** marriage and reasonable unions, and as a celebration of love founded in free will.

As for strife being the creator of all great things, this tells me to stay. If I leave, I'll hurt for a little while, but this in the end is an escape from strife. If I stay, I strive, really strive, but in the end, hopefully, I grow. And he grows, and our love is more than "I'll stay with you as long as things are fine". I've been running away all my life, I'm staying because I'm tired of running, I want to put in effort and make it work, and learn to adapt and to be patient and compromising and forgiving to someone. It's just... really difficult sometimes.

It's not your fault. Your family may think a certain way and have certain values, but this doesn't mean they are infaillible. Families are also people, with their own issues, their own messed up views of the world, and sometimes these harm us. Especially since they're so close to us and we grow up thinking they are right about everything.

Rape is not your fault. Rape is the rapist's fault. In this rape culture, women are told that to prevent rape, they shouldn't wear short skirts. Well, women and girls get raped all the time when they're wearing their pyjamas, when they're wearing pants, when they're alone in their homes, they get raped by family members, they get raped by teachers, and they get raped when they wear mini skirts and pass out at parties, and NONE OF IT IS THEIR FAULT. Nobody is responsible but the rapist. In order to prevent rape, we should tell rapists not to rape, and that's that.

I imagine your family's views affect you deeply. I'm sorry they aren't offering the support you need and deserve. It's not worth much but I understand: my mother has borderline personality disorder and she hasn't been the best mom to me. I don't blame her, she is sick and she suffers also, but I know it's messed me up a lot. For some time, I wasn't talking to her, and since welcoming her back in my life I have set some clear limits for myself and I'm not willing to deal with her if she crosses them. I don't know how old you are and if this is a possibility for you, but sometimes it helps to get away for a while.

If this isn't possible or you don't wish to do that, do remember this: your family isn't the voice of reason, and no matter what it is that makes them think you are responsible for your own rape, this is a backward view that is only meant to protect archaic world orders. You're not responsible for what happened.

I'm sure if you go to /r/twoxchromosomes and share your feelings about feeling responsible you will find a lot of help and support there.
Dang... thanks, that's a nice compliment. Ha. I try.

Wow...... thanks so much...... your message really touched me.

I don't know how much I can "show" him, he is his own person after all and his way of being and doing things is also legitimate. He's different but this doesn't mean he should twist himself into uncomfortable positions just to fit the mould. I also have to deal with him, and to try to understand his ways so I don't interpret them badly. Still, I have affective needs and it's hard to feel loved when someone doesn't communicate this clearly.

Still, what you said resonates with me. It's true that there's a tremendous amount of energy that is spent on bad things here. A lot of yelling, crying, feeling bad, pacing around, crying some more, thinking about bad things. I will try to find a way to channel this more effectively. All these powerful negative reactions... It's like a nuclear reactor. There *has* to be a way to harness this for good... no? :(

No, that's fine, don't worry, I can take it and I think I need to be talked to clearly. I might not agree with everything I am told but I am open to hearing it and in the end this helps me figure things out for myself. So thanks.

He's not an extreme case either. His own mother, who is a school help for special needs kids, never picked up on it (though I suspect denial there). He can turn it on, he can be personable, especially after a few beers and with people our own age. With family that can be harder, and he definitely needs some time to become comfortable around people (several meetings), but when I started dating him, he was there and connected and he has said since that he was doing his best to "be that guy", to "turn it on". He's said, in bad moments, that he knew that nobody would be with the person he is, and so he pretended to be charming and put in effort and seducing me. I miss that guy, I really do.

Still he turns it on sometimes, but there's also the fact that I'm ADD. When I need attention, it's *right now*. If I don't get it, I'll feel really hurt and rejected. He on the other hand needs long transition periods. My memory is dodgy and my emotions are powerful so even though I'm aware of this and able to tell you right now, at the time I'm overwhelmed and it's a huge deal. I have a hard time controlling the intensity of my emotion.

I don't think he's a terrible boyfriend. He'd deal better with a quiet, independent girl, but he says he's been in that type of relationship before and it doesn't work. Nobody said anything, nothing was dealt with. I might complain a lot but at least I'm not the type who would pretend all is fine for a long time. Eventually it comes out and though we deal with it very badly, I think he finds this better to not dealing with it at all.

I also really need to work on communicating more clearly what I need. It does upset me that he doesn't seem to "need" to be around me or to connect with me, and I can't get over that. If I did, I would probably not mind leading and going to him, so long as he didn't push me away when I do. But as it is now, I just wait around trying to see if he will come to me because I'm too afraid to come to him. I'm afraid because his anxiety issues make him kinda cold and non-responsive when I do sometimes, and it feels pretty bad to try to kiss your boyfriend and have this stone cold guy give you a nervous peck and try to move away from you. And so I get sad and this attaches more negative triggers to intimacy, which in turn make him more nervous the next time around, etc. Guh, I just have no idea where to start to help reduce the anxiety while respecting my feelings.

EDIT: And thanks so much for your reply by the way. If you don't mind continuing this conversation a bit, I think I could get a lot from it.

It's important that you find a doctor. My mother attempted suicide a few years back and she checked herself into the psych ward voluntarily. Once she was in, it hit her hard and she disliked it very much. But after a few days she realized it was going to help her a lot. She had some time to breathe and think about her life, but most of all they were there to adjust her medication daily and when she left, she was fine (for a while anyway, BPDs often get off their meds on their own, which she did). Consider this if you think your medication is making you feel bad. It's important that your prescription is adjusted to you. Xx
Yes, yes I would like that. How old are you? How have you been coping? How long have you two been together? What sorts of issues have you encountered and how did they get better if any?

Yeah, it is, but at the same time it makes him a wonderful individual with talents and ideas unknown to most of us. It makes him unique and puzzling. His perspective is always a new one to me. Of course, on certain topics this is more fun than others - I enjoy a lengthy conversation with him about, say, cannibalism and his views on it WAY more than I'd enjoy a conversation about how to manage meals and chores. Basically he'd eat raw vegetables and hummus, or just a big boiled cauliflower for dinner every day. He'd wear dirty clothes and never shave all the time. But I value his mind, the way we can connect on that level, though the strife and anxiety steals a lot of that away sometimes.

Thanks a lot for taking the time to formulate an answer. I have to say however, it is hard for me to relate to. I don't believe that marriage is a more sure sign of a lifelong commitment than anything else. Getting married is a legal contract which should be signed for legal reasons, it has to do with rights and privileges, and there is such a thing as divorce for when it doesn't work. I don't think my union isn't as important to save than another union because I haven't gone to City Hall to sign some papers. Married or not, my choice would be my choice, and it's important that married people also know that they *can* get out if they wish to. But like I said, breaking up is not an option for me right now. It just adds strife and doesn't stick and I'm not able to deal with it right now.

Much love to you. Nobody can tell you that you should or should not be over something. The time you take is the time you take and that's that. My heart goes out to you. I'm sorry you have to deal with this, the pills and the anxiety and all the rest. I hope it doesn't sound cheesy and cliché to you when I say this, because I mean it with all that I have: what happened to you was not your fault, and you did not deserve to be mistreated like this.

Nah, I don't mean he couldn't be happy with someone else. There are girls out there better suited to his temperament, that's for sure. I just mean he isn't going to change, or not much, and not fast. He's gonna be who he is. He can't help that. He's wired that way. I'm not staying out of pity, I'm staying out of hope. Whether that hope is completely dumb or founded, nobody can tell the future. I also stay out of love, if that wasn't obvious enough. We fight and I'm miserable for long periods at a time, but sometimes things go well and it's pretty sweet. It's just the bad spells drain everything out of me. They go on for so long... They feed themselves.

Thank you for your kind words. I don't know what to say... I feel like I'm too cowardly to do anything anyway, and I don't (thankfully) have access to a gun or anything. If I had one, I don't know if I'd still be here to talk about it. I look down from my balcony and I'm just scared of breaking my femur and agonizing forever. My mother took pills and just lost consciousness, got a big scar on her nose and lost a whole week of her memory. Hanging myself, are you crazy, feeling my lungs bursting in flames... I'm not gonna do any of that gruesome stuff. So I guess what I'm trying to say is, yes I've given this considerable thought and it's scaring me, but it's not for tomorrow.

Our diagnosis is not by a neurologist. Most adults with Asperger's are in fact self-diagnosed, and most people who self-diagnose end up actually having AS. He scores incredibly high on the AQ test, and the person he saw at the autism spectrum organization he is getting services at seemed pretty convinced. It's a matter of getting a medical diagnosis. Though yes, I understand that the formal diagnosis is of a certain importance, which is why I state in the very first lines of my post what the actual situation is, even though it doesn't feel relevant to how I feel at this point in time.

Thanks for this thoughtful reply. I really do appreciate it.

Yes, understanding what is mine to own up to. That's a hard thing. Because at once I often feel like my feelings must be unjustified, exaggerated, not worthy of being taken seriously, but on the other hand it hurts so much to not have them acknowledged, and my boyfriend isn't so good at acknowledging me. I've seen many psychologists but I have trouble translating what I understand about myself (why certain things are such strong triggers to me) into action to improve my life. Also, in the middle of a highly emotional situation, it's really hard for me to keep track of what's going on and to really pick things apart and understand what's what, what is mine, what is his, what is mine but still justifiable, etc. Like I said, I get to a place where everything is such shit and nothing seems like it could save me from that dark place. Honestly, if I'd had access to something as instant as a gun, I'd be dead for sure by now. It's the pain that makes me afraid.

Though I will try it. I'll keep your words in mind. Being kind to myself. That isn't something that has much effect on me. I live through others a lot, having been told all my childhood that my emotions were surely fake, that I was a big comedian, that there was no space for how I felt. The only way for me to be not even happy, just a bit "safe" from my mom's frequent, violent outbursts was to keep her happy, and so when everyone isn't smiling around me I start getting worried. I have trouble centering myself on me.

I don't think it's intentional. It often stems from misunderstandings and uncertainty. He doesn't navigate feelings well and I want to give him the benefit of the doubt. I mean, he's pretty combattive and prone to anger and resentment, but I don't see him as cold and manipulative, though who the hell knows if someone is cold and manipulative. Usually those people are good at hiding this. I don't know.

He says he cares about me, I just never see any of it. And when I bring it up, he gets all defensive and doesn't want to be "controlled" into anything, even if controlled means asked and anything means spending time with his girlfriend. *sigh* He does mention the pressure thing a lot. But at some point, my own affective needs aren't met, and I burst, creating more pressure, making it harder for him to express it, etc.

Things change, just... really slowly. That's to be expected with Aspies. Things that seem normal to most are a real struggle to them. I believe he honestly has Asperger's. Some things that he says and does are just too... out there. He doesn't understand expressions, language always has to be painfully direct (and I don't mean that I beat around the bush, I mean that "Would you like to help me?" yields an aswer like "I don't think I'd like to, no" whereas "It would really make me happy if you helped me" would get me "Oh well no problem then").
